title: Gadsden Purchase
summary: The United States bought a strip of northern Mexican territory, now southern Arizona and southern New Mexico, for $10 million. James Gadsden and Santa Anna signed a treaty on 30 December 1853, and a revised version was ratified in 1854. It enabled a southern railroad route and set the present southern border.

as_recorded.value: Santa Anna, who signed it on June 8,

where.modern_name: Southern Arizona and southern New Mexico

importance.justification: It fixed the southern border of the present-day contiguous United States and enabled a southern railroad route.

reviewer_note: Sources differ on the original treaty terms: Britannica gives $10 million and nearly 30,000 square miles for the purchase, while the State Department says the signed treaty offered $15 million for 45,000 square miles before revision. The end date relies on Santa Anna's signing of the revised treaty on 8 June 1854; the Senate ratified on 25 April 1854.}</br> (Drafted by the Wikipedia pipeline from Encyclopaedia Britannica, U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian; quotes machine-checked.)
